correctness.rationale: Under the specified height-two relations, adjacent comparable pairs in any extension are disjoint cover edges, so they form a matching of the path of labels. At even order its perfect matching forces one descending block word; at odd order each unmatched odd label creates two forced block chains with binomially many shuffles. The first two positions and only those yield a neighbor within the odd optimum stratum. This proves the exact degree, multiplicity and matching. The explicit opposite order pair proves the diameter bound. Two distinct exhaustive verifiers agree for n<=11 and n<=13 respectively; finite tests are corroborative, not the all-parameter proof.

originality.rationale: The public primary paper Bondarenko (2011) and scholarly database comparisons establish that degree-as-jumps, general linear-extension graph connectivity and enumeration algorithms are established, but the full text checked does not cover the fence-specific parity law for the minimum-degree vertex count and its exact induced matching. Four specific implication comparisons were made, not mere title matching. The general Naatz (2000) paper could be inspected only by publisher abstract and leaves a stated residual risk; nothing in that abstract logically implies the asserted extremal census. This is a qualified self-review best-knowledge PASS, not a uniqueness certificate.

value.rationale: The result gives an exact structural classification of the least-mobile portion of a natural all-size graph of permutation schedules. Its exceptional parity produces an exponential jump in minimizer number, yet the optimal stratum itself is only disjoint edges; this supplies geometry beyond classic jump-number and Gray-code feasibility. The induced-subgraph description can inform constrained search from jump-optimal starting schedules.
